topic: Static CMOS and the NAND cell
title: Build XOR from four NAND cells
instructions:
## Why chips are built from NAND

A static CMOS NAND gate needs only four transistors: two PMOS in parallel in the pull-up network and two NMOS in series in the pull-down network. An XOR built directly in CMOS needs more transistors and slower pass structures. That is why standard-cell libraries lean on NAND, and why NAND is called a **universal** gate.

## Do this

Build **Y = A XOR B** using **only NAND gates**, at most four of them. Place switches A and B and an output lamp Y, then wire the gates.

The classic construction: N1 = NAND(A, B), N2 = NAND(A, N1), N3 = NAND(B, N1), Y = NAND(N2, N3).

When it works, count the transistors: four NAND cells at four transistors each.
hints: Start with one NAND fed by A and B. Its output feeds two more NANDs.
The second NAND takes A and N1. The third takes B and N1.
The last NAND combines the second and third.

checks.label: Uses at most four NAND gates

realityNote: Four NAND cells come to 16 transistors. A good transmission-gate XOR does it with 8, which is why libraries also ship a dedicated XOR cell and synthesis tools choose between them by area and delay.
